edit.description: the bare rethrow of a slot leg's error once every slot has settled
the carry that wraps a `PendingParseFailure` alone widens to every cause, in a class it does not have to invent a ledger verdict for
`tick()`'s catch admits the carried verdict without reading it as a ledger refusal
a wave that shipped spans and then lost a slot leg outside a ledger read

summary: A slot leg's throw outside a ledger read tears the wave down with no verdict — every landed span's recovery sha and the tick's whole usage go unwritten

per.section: The tick verdict — one facts artifact

acceptance: every throw out of a slot's own leg — an agent that exploded, a hook that threw, a render that did not resolve — leaves the settled wave's verdict on disk carrying the spans already on trunk and a usage row per agent that ran, the way the mid-wave ledger read's own refusal already does; a cause that is no ledger refusal is reported as none, and the exit class a non-ledger slot throw takes is the harness error it takes today, so no supervisor-child contract moves
tests: a wave whose slot leg throws outside a ledger read still writes the settled wave's verdict
the verdict a wave writes after a slot leg throws names every span it landed on trunk
notes: Field-measured (loop of 2026-09-28T22:59Z): 61 build agent results in the log against one build row in `tick-verdicts.jsonl`, ~$204 unaccounted, spans intact. `waveReadRefusal` (`src/waveMerge.ts`) returns any non-`PendingParseFailure` unwrapped; `src/waveTick.ts` throws it bare past every settled slot; `tick()`'s catch rethrows what is neither error class. The render arm that fired it this run is a separate question — `spec/prompt.md` states placeholder-failure semantics as an open gap.
